speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. Given your gait and limb ataxia, have you noticed any recent changes in your vision, such as blurred or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs, or any trouble with your speech and swallowing? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature Normothermic, Blood Pressure Within normal range, Heart Rate Within normal range, Respiratory Rate Within normal range. Neurological Examination: Gait Assessment shows ataxic gait, Right Upper Limb Strength is 4/5, Coordination Tests show evidence of ataxia. MRI Brain: Findings show lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML); T1/T2 images show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Given the MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement and the clinical presentation of subacute gait and limb ataxia, this is highly suggestive of JC virus reactivation. Did you have a known immunocompromised condition, such as HIV/AIDS, or are you currently on immunosuppressive therapy like natalizumab?
